_meta.indication: PORTRAZZA is an EGFR antagonist indicated, in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin, for first-line treatment of patients with metastatic squamous non-small cell lung cancer; not indicated for non-squamous NSCLC.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), multicenter, open-label, controlled trial comparing PORTRAZZA plus gemcitabine and cisplatin to gemcitabine and cisplatin alone.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed Stage IV squamous NSCLC in the first-line metastatic setting.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (OS) was the primary efficacy endpoint; PFS and ORR were secondary.
pivotal_trials.result: Median OS 11.5 vs 9.9 months; stratified HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.74, 0.96); p=0.012. PFS HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74, 0.98); p=0.02; median PFS 5.7 vs 5.5 months.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were rash (44%), vomiting (29%), diarrhea (16%), and dermatitis acneiform (15%). Hypomagnesemia occurred in 83% (severe in 20%). Serious toxicities included cardiopulmonary arrest/sudden death (3% vs 0.6%) and venous thromboembolic events (9% vs 5%).
target_moa: Necitumumab is a recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the human epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), blocks binding of EGFR to its ligands, and induces EGFR internalization and degradation.
modality: mAb (recombinant human IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: CARDIOPULMONARY ARREST and HYPOMAGNESEMIA — cardiopulmonary arrest and/or sudden death occurred in 3% of patients; hypomagnesemia occurred in 83% (severe in 20%). Monitor electrolytes with aggressive replacement during and after PORTRAZZA.

advisory_committee.vote: ODAC convened July 9, 2015; the majority of the committee agreed that the efficacy and safety results of SQUIRE support a positive benefit:risk assessment of necitumumab in combination with gemcitabine/cisplatin in the proposed population.

orphan_indication.text: On November 20, 2015, FDA granted orphan drug designation for necitumumab for the treatment of squamous, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

citations.quote: On November 20, 2015, FDA granted orphan drug designation for necitumumab for the “treatment of squamous, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).”

basis.text: Lilly requested priority review designation, but the application was reviewed as Standard.

citations.quote: On October 22, 2014, Lilly submitted the first component of BLA 125547, containing Module 4, associated sections of Module 2, administrative items in Module 1, and in support of the nonclinical reproductive toxicity assessment, authorization to a cross reference BLA 125084 in support of BLA 125547, and request for priority review designation.

summary.text: PORTRAZZA was approved as a standard-review BLA (priority review requested but denied) supported by the single pivotal SQUIRE trial; FDA convened ODAC (July 9, 2015) to weigh the modest OS benefit (HR 0.84) against toxicity; orphan drug designation was granted for squamous NSCLC on November 20, 2015. It was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: This application is primarily supported by the efficacy and safety results of a single study, SQUIRE (I4X-IE-JFCC, IMCL CP11-0806).
This BLA was referred to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) for advice and presented on July 9, 2015.

The pivotal study, SQUIRE for squamous NSCLC, met its primary efficacy objective statistically. The addition of necitumumab to gemcitabine and cisplatin demonstrated a 1.6 month improvement in median OS [HR=0.84 (95% CI 0.74, 0.96); two-sided log-rank p=0.012].
On November 20, 2015, FDA granted orphan drug designation for necitumumab for the “treatment of squamous, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).”
